source_name: ВУЕ (Велика українська енциклопедія) — «Акти Національного банку України нормативно-правові»
why_relevant: State encyclopaedia entry defining the taxonomy of NBU acts (постанови, положення, інструкції), their binding force and the statutory publication/effective-date rules — the authoritative glossary for building the classification schema of this cell.

source_name: Міністерство юстиції України — офіційні періодичні видання (regional Minjust explainers)
why_relevant: Regional Ministry of Justice offices publish plain-language explanations of which publications count as official, what the legal effect of publication is, and what the chronological/alphabetical indices to the gazette are. Useful for encoding correct deadline rules into the collection pipeline rather than guessing.

source_name: NBU Resolution No.143 of 09.12.2025 — Regulation on information security and cyber defence measures by financial service providers (zakon.rada.gov.ua)
why_relevant: The current binding rulebook for non-bank financial service providers (finance companies, insurers, credit unions, pawnshops), in force from mid-December 2025 with a compliance horizon reported as end-2026. DORA-aligned. A hard-deadline document that drives procurement of security tooling.

source_name: Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No.712 of 18.06.2025 — procedure for developing/approving security profiles and security authorisation (kmu.gov.ua)
why_relevant: Implements Law 4336-IX: defines basic, sectoral and target security profiles (basic profiles approved by SSSCIP) and the security-authorisation procedure. Sectoral profiles are the mechanism by which banking/payment infrastructure gets its own binding technical baseline and dates.

source_name: АМКУ — payments/acquiring market investigations and market studies (PrivatBank / Oschadbank acquiring & interchange)
why_relevant: AMCU has run a multi-year abuse-of-dominance investigation into merchant acquiring and interchange involving the two largest state banks, and publishes draft amendments to the Положення про концентрацію. Directly shapes PSP/acquirer economics — a competition-side regulatory risk invisible on NBU domains.

source_name: zakon.rada.gov.ua — NBU register regulations (Положення про реєстрацію платіжних систем, учасників та технологічних операторів)
why_relevant: Official legal database entry for the amendments to the NBU regulation governing what goes into the Register of Payment Infrastructure and on what timetable. Defines the register's fields, inclusion/exclusion grounds and statutory deadlines — required to interpret register diffs correctly rather than guessing.

source_name: Кабінет Міністрів України — Методика проведення аналізу впливу регуляторного акта НБУ
why_relevant: The binding methodology that dictates what an NBU RIA must contain (problem definition, alternatives, mechanism, expected results, effectiveness indicators, tracking measures). Reference document for parsing and normalising the analiz_*.pdf files — it tells the analyst which fields are always present.

source_name: Cabinet of Ministers news — SEPA accession communications
why_relevant: Official Ukrainian framing and timing of the SEPA track ('фінансовий безвіз'), including adoption of the draft-law package (17 Dec 2025). Provides the domestic-side dates to pair with EPC-side decisions.

source_name: NBU Board Resolution No. 80 of 25.07.2025 — Regulation on Open Banking in Ukraine (official PDF)
why_relevant: The foundational open banking secondary act: defines ASPSP/TPP duties, consent, data-exchange requirements and the compliance clock (ASPSPs given five months; API technical specification to be approved within 18 months). Core deadline-bearing document for the cell.

source_name: Law of Ukraine No.4336-IX of 27.03.2025 — amendments on information protection and cyber defence of state information resources and CII objects
why_relevant: The framework statute that reformatted Ukraine's cyber-defence system, replacing the old KSZI/complex-protection paradigm with security profiles and security authorisation. Everything SSSCIP now imposes on CII operators, banks included, derives from it.

source_name: NBU Resolution No.69 of 27.06.2025 — Critical infrastructure of the financial sector (amending Regulation No.178 on cyber defence in the banking system)
why_relevant: Unifies criteria for designating critical infrastructure objects across the financial sector and amends the 2022 banking cyber-defence regulation. Determines which banks/PSPs fall under the heavier SSSCIP-linked obligations.

source_name: НБУ — draft resolutions published as PDFs under /admin_uploads
why_relevant: Draft and final resolution texts are served as static PDFs under predictable /admin_uploads/article/ and /admin_uploads/law/ paths; these static assets are often reachable when the HTML pages are WAF-blocked, and contain the operative 'ця постанова набирає чинності з ...' clause.

source_name: NBU Board Resolution No. 81 of 25.07.2025 — authorisation of non-financial payment service providers (TPPs)
why_relevant: Sets the three authorisation routes for AIS/PIS providers (non-PSP legal entities, payment institutions, e-money institutions, foreign PI branches, banks) — the gate every fintech TPP must pass, with a 31.12.2025 registration deadline and a 01.01.2027 professional-indemnity-insurance step-up.

source_name: NBU Resolution No.95 of 28.09.2017 — Regulation on information security measures in the banking system (zakon.rada.gov.ua)
why_relevant: The baseline ISMS regulation for Ukrainian banks (ISO 27001-style requirements, phased implementation). A March-2025 draft replacement was published for consultation, so the pair (in-force act + draft successor) shows the direction of travel and future deadlines.

source_name: NBU Open Banking Concept 2023 (КОНЦЕПЦІЯ відкритого банкінгу)
why_relevant: Explicitly not a normative act, but sets out the NBU's design intent, roadmap phases and Berlin Group alignment that the 2025 resolutions operationalise — indispensable for interpreting later acts and anticipating the API specification.

source_name: NBU Resolution No.24 of 2025 — amendments to NBU acts on information security and cyber defence
why_relevant: Amendment package touching several NBU information-security/cyber acts at once; the kind of omnibus change that silently resets compliance dates for banks and PSPs.

source_name: НБУ Стратегія / strategy and supervisory methodology PDFs
why_relevant: The NBU strategy document sets the multi-year direction (EU acquis alignment, Basel implementation) from which future prudential resolutions and their transition timetables derive — context for anticipating deadlines rather than recording them.

source_name: НБУ — форма надання зауважень та пропозицій (shablon_propozyciy.xlsx)
why_relevant: The mandatory comment-submission template linked from every consultation notice. It documents the formal channel and the metadata the NBU expects from respondents — useful for understanding who can respond and how, and for a client that may want to file comments.

source_name: MONEYVAL Strategy 2023-2027 — unofficial Ukrainian translation (MoF)
why_relevant: Sets the evaluation cycle and methodology Ukraine will be judged under in the next round; the Ukrainian translation is the authoritative source of local terminology used by supervised institutions.

source_name: NISS (Національний інститут стратегічних досліджень) — analyses of World Bank Group support to Ukraine
why_relevant: State-affiliated think tank summarising the structure and conditions of World Bank Group support — helpful for mapping which operations carry financial-sector conditions and how the Ukrainian side frames them.

source_name: НБУ — Білі книги та консультаційні документи (White Papers / discussion papers)
why_relevant: The pre-legislative tier: before drafting a postanova the NBU publishes a 'біла книга' or 'консультаційний документ' setting out its intended regulatory concept and invites market feedback. This is 12–24 months of lead time on the eventual binding rule (examples: non-bank leasing regulation, ESG management, AI use in the financial sector).

source_name: NBU news item — updated conduct-supervision procedure (Актуалізовано порядок нагляду ...)
why_relevant: Concrete example of the regulator announcing a change to the conduct-supervision framework — extending it to limited payment service providers and ethical-behaviour requirements. Exactly the 'next tightening' signal the cell is meant to catch, and shows the announcement pattern to monitor.

source_name: НКЦПФР — Аналітична довідка про роботу Комісії та стан ринків капіталу (quarterly analytical reports, PDF)
why_relevant: Quarterly official statistics and enforcement/licensing activity on capital and organised commodity markets — gives supervisory intensity trend, not just individual acts. PDFs are served from a predictable wp-content path.

source_name: NBU Regulation No.178 of 12.08.2022 — Organisation of cyber defence in the banking system of Ukraine (ipLex mirror)
why_relevant: The core banking cyber-defence regulation and companion to the 2017 information-security regulation; defines critical infrastructure objects in the banking system and incident-reporting duties. ipLex is a usable mirror when rada.gov.ua is rate-limited.

source_name: OTP Bank Ukraine — legal PDFs (approved-by-order documents)
why_relevant: Terms documents carry 'Затверджено наказом №… від …' headers, letting an analyst date internal approval versus public effective date — a proxy for how long the bank took to implement a rule.

source_name: FinTech Ukraine Forum 2026 — press release / agenda coverage (Interfax-Ukraine press-release wire)
why_relevant: Organiser-issued press release describing the 2026 forum (AUB-organised, Kyiv, 29 May) with the framing 'євроінтеграція, цифровізація та ШІ у фокусі' — names the regulatory themes and the regulator/government participants. Interfax's press-release channel is a general pointer to Ukrainian financial-event announcements, not just this one.

source_name: Меморандум про забезпечення прозорості функціонування ринку платіжних послуг (industry memorandum coordinated by AUB + NABU)
why_relevant: Textbook self-regulation artefact: banks, coordinated by the banking associations, signed and later (14 May 2026) updated a Memorandum setting common approaches to client work and transfer limits for ФОП/companies to counter illegal financial schemes. Sets de-facto compliance deadlines for members outside formal NBU regulation — high-value for the deadlines topic. Mirrored on both NABU and AUB sites.

source_name: CMU Resolution No.518 of 19.06.2019 — General requirements for cyber defence of critical infrastructure objects (LigaZakon copy)
why_relevant: The baseline 'Загальні вимоги до кіберзахисту об'єктів критичної інфраструктури' that banks as CI operators must meet; updated versions impose mandatory basic measures, continuous cyber-risk management, a cybersecurity plan, staff training and funding. Directly generates compliance-driven demand.

source_name: National FinMon Forum (Ukrainian Compliance Association + LIGA ZAKON) — AML/compliance conference circuit
why_relevant: Compliance-side conference where regulators, lawmakers, systemic-bank compliance officers and international lawyers preview incoming EU-driven financial-monitoring requirements (money mules, new EU AML package). Supervision/AML rules are a large slice of A3 and this circuit is distinct from the payments/fintech one.

source_name: European Payments Council — Criteria for the extension of the SEPA geographical scope
why_relevant: The formal, EPC-Board-approved criteria a non-EEA community (i.e. Ukraine) must satisfy to enter SEPA scheme geographic scope, plus the periodic continuous-compliance review. Defines the exact conditions driving Ukraine's AML/PSD-alignment legislative package.

source_name: EEAS / Council — EU-Ukraine Association Agenda and Association Council conclusions
why_relevant: The Association Agenda is the negotiated short-list of priority reforms, and Association Council / Association Committee in Trade Configuration outcomes formally record financial-services commitments and their timing. The 10th Association Council met 9 Apr 2025.

source_name: sud.ua — legal-sector news on NBU draft regulations
why_relevant: Ukrainian legal news outlet that reports NBU draft resolutions (e.g. changes to the banking-secrecy disclosure rules) while they are still in consultation, often summarising the substantive change faster than the official notice is parsed.

source_name: Ukrainian competition-law firm merger-control guides (Asters, VKP, Chambers, GCR)
why_relevant: Annually refreshed English-language restatements of AMCU thresholds, the special one-tenth-of-assets rule for banks, filing timelines and Phase I/II statistics. Fastest way to get a defensible baseline of Ukrainian merger-clearance burden on banks without parsing Ukrainian statute.

source_name: Baker McKenzie — Global Financial Services Regulatory Guide, Ukraine chapter
why_relevant: A maintained, question-structured reference on Ukrainian licensing/authorisation ('what is the process for becoming authorized') rather than a news feed — the right source for baseline regulatory-perimeter facts against which new alerts are diffed. Kyiv office regulatory team (incl. financial monitoring, currency, capital controls) backs it.

source_name: Deloitte Ukraine — tax and legal alerts (cyber/data compliance for financial institutions)
why_relevant: Big-four alerts translate NBU/SSSCIP acts into scoped obligations and compliance dates for financial institutions, and flag DORA alignment. High signal on what regulated entities will actually have to buy and by when.

source_name: finance.ua / finclub.net — financial media tracking NBU regulatory moves
why_relevant: Ukrainian financial media report NBU consultations with the comment deadline stated explicitly (e.g. draft amendments to the account opening/closing Instruction, comments accepted to 10 Aug 2026) and cover industry pushback on effective dates.

source_name: KPMG Ukraine / Big Four regulatory alerts (uk)
why_relevant: Professional-services alerts translate a new NBU resolution into the concrete compliance obligation and the date by which banks/payment providers must comply — a useful interpretation layer and a redundancy signal that a resolution was adopted.

source_name: Oschadbank — ДКБО and consumer-information PDFs (uploads directory)
why_relevant: The dated ДКБО and 'Загальна інформація для споживачів фінансових послуг' PDFs carry a valid-from date in the filename, giving a machine-readable timeline of when regulatory-driven terms took effect.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine — оголошення PDFs (storage/files) on tariff & rules changes
why_relevant: Standalone 'оголошення' PDFs state which Rules/Tariffs change and the exact date they take effect (e.g. from 26.06.2025, from 02.10). Highest-density source of implementation dates for this bank.

source_name: UKRSIBBANK — News posts on service-condition changes
why_relevant: BNP Paribas-affiliated bank posts dated announcements changing card/savings and acquiring conditions; useful for comparing a foreign-owned group's implementation timing against domestic peers.

source_name: UKRSIBBANK — legal_documents PDF repository (order-numbered rules)
why_relevant: Rules PDFs are captioned 'Додаток N до Наказу від DD.MM.YYYY № H-LEG-YYYY-NN', giving an unusually precise, serialised internal-change log that can be tracked over time.

source_name: Wolf Theiss / Kinstellar / Ilyashev law-firm payments briefings (Ukraine)
why_relevant: Law firms are the fastest reliable English-language interpreters of NBU resolution numbers, authorisation routes and compliance dates; they name the exact resolutions (No. 80, No. 81 of 25.07.2025) that are hard to pin down from the regulator's site alone.

source_name: Ukrainian general business/finance press covering open banking go-live (RBC-Ukraine, Censor.net BIZ, Mind.ua, dev.ua, Minfin)
why_relevant: Carries dated statements of go-live expectations (API opening from 01.08.2025; full technical readiness no later than 01.08.2026; system-wide readiness expected Aug-Sep 2026) and NBU officials' remarks that do not always appear in formal acts.

source_name: EU4Digital — Ukraine critical infrastructure cybersecurity alignment with EU standards
why_relevant: EU-funded programme reporting on Ukraine's NIS2/DORA-direction alignment and donor-funded capacity building. Useful for anticipating which EU instruments Ukrainian rules will copy next and where donor money for security tooling is flowing.

source_name: EUR-Lex — Commission Staff Working Document, Ukraine Report (SWD(2025) 759 final)
why_relevant: The annual Ukraine country report is the single densest statement of what Ukraine must still align (CRR/CRD, BRRD, DGSD, capital markets acquis) and how prepared it is. EUR-Lex gives stable CELEX identifiers, making year-on-year diffing of the financial-services chapter mechanical.

entity_name: Legalink / Lexology legal alerts on Ukraine's new cybersecurity law
source_name: Legalink / Lexology legal alerts on Ukraine's new cybersecurity law
why_relevant: English-language law-firm analysis of Law 4336-IX naming SSSCIP's powers (basic and sectoral security profiles, incident repository, supervision) — the fastest way to brief non-Ukrainian-speaking stakeholders and to map obligations onto payment operators.

source_name: U.S.-Ukraine Business Council (USUBC) — Ukraine regulatory notices
why_relevant: A foreign business association republishing NBU draft-regulation notices in English. Useful as an English-language mirror of consultation launches and as a pointer to the international-business counterparties in Ukrainian consultations.

source_name: Ukraine Fintech Week — recap and speaker coverage (Scroll.media)
why_relevant: Event recaps are the practical substitute for missing transcripts: they report what NBU/IMF/World Bank speakers actually said on stage, including forward-looking regulatory statements that appear nowhere in official releases.

source_name: Ukrgasbank — public offer / rules documents and unilateral-amendment acts
why_relevant: State bank publishing 'односторонній правочин' amendment acts with explicit effective dates; complements the private-bank sample for state-vs-private implementation-timing comparison.
